one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events probably fall in the window. (1) Q3 2026 earnings: data vendors estimate Thu 2026-10-29 before the open, but the IR calendar has not confirmed it yet (prior years: Oct 30 2025, Oct 31 2024). The window ends Oct 30, so I put the odds of the print landing inside it at about 85-90%. Consensus is about $4.99 EPS on $10.86B revenue. Quanta beat and raised in Q1 and Q2. Correction from round 1: the stock did not fall after the Q2 beat. It closed +17.3% on Jul 30 ($561.14 to $657.98) and kept rising to $722.31 on Aug 17. The ~16% slide to $603.78 came Aug 17-25, weeks later, on worries about leverage and valuation (Twelve Data daily closes). Earnings-day moves are large in both directions (+17% Q2-26, about -2.5% Q3-25), so the print widens the distribution more than it tilts it. (2) FOMC on Oct 27-28: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16. Kalshi is about 65% hold / 33-35% hike as of Oct 1-2, after softer August PCE. A hike would weigh on a ~34x-forward multiple. The 30-day revisions (24 up, 0 down) and the history of beats give a small upward tilt, offset by the rates risk. I centre at about $670 with lognormal sigma 13.5%: the usual 12.6% monthly vol (44%/3.5), widened for an earnings print plus an FOMC meeting in the same window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (50%), EV/EBITDA (30%) and FCF yield (20%), all on the next-twelve-months view as of Oct 2027. NTM EPS of about $22.4 x 30x gives $672; NTM EBITDA of $5.4B x 20x less $5.9B net debt gives $670; 2028 FCF of $3.2B at a 3.0% yield gives $700. Blended: about $677. Versus round 1: net debt goes up, the backlog fact changes to +49% (which supports estimates), and the 30x multiple is now justified by rates and peers rather than the discounted ROIC claim.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus x ~1.18. 12-month backlog is $32.3B, +61% YoY, and total backlog is +49% YoY (Q2 8-K), which supports high-teens growth. The NiSource program is still mostly outside backlog. Hyperscaler capex consensus is about $1.1T in 2027, +~35% (UBS sees ~25% growth; the 54% figure is Goldman's above-consensus view). Direct data-center exposure is only ~10% of revenue, so slowing hyperscaler capex in 2028 is a second-order hit. Revelio active job postings (+52% in 2026) are consistent with the company hiring to staff a backlog that is ~49% larger, not just replacing departures.

It trades at about 34x NTM today, down from 50x on June 30. Peers: Comfort Systems 31x, EMCOR 22x, MasTec 19x (TIKR). The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026, and 12 of 18 participants see one more hike in 2026, a headwind for long-duration multiples. I assume compression to about FIX's level, 30x. Round 1 also cited the Substack ROIC of 6-8%. The supervisor discounted that claim as unverified, and it no longer drives the multiple.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$5.4B x 20x = $108B EV, less ~$5.9B net debt, over 152.4M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.15B midpoint, grown about 16% in 2027 (in line with consensus revenue of $45.7B vs $39.6B) and about 14% in 2028, then time-weighted.

The 424B5 pro forma shows $7.0B debt and $1.4B cash, so ~$5.6B net at 6/30/26; the August notes repaid CP and the revolver. Add the July Enerfab payment (it closed after June 30) and continuing M&A of about $1.2B a year, funded by FCF, to get about $5.9B.
Today's EV of about $106.6B over NTM EBITDA of about $4.65B is roughly 23x. I apply the same compression as in the P/E method.
$2.25B midpoint compounded at about 19%/yr, in line with EBITDA growth plus margin. A FCF margin of about 6-7% of revenue matches the history in Doroshenko's piece.
The current yield is about 2.1% (2026 FCF midpoint over a $101B market cap). As growth slows and rates rise (Fed at 3.75-4.00%), I let it normalise toward 3%.

bear.story: Hyperscalers digest AI capex in 2027 (UBS already sees growth slowing to ~25%), or financing trouble at the neoclouds slows load growth. The Fed keeps hiking past 4.25%, and integration problems at the acquired businesses hurt margins. EPS lands at about $19.5 and the multiple falls toward 22-23x, in line with EMCOR. I no longer use the thin Polymarket recession market (~$9.7k volume) to size this case. Instead it rests on rates and the capex cycle.

base.story: Backlog of $53.4B (+49% YoY; 12-month backlog +61%) converts, and Quanta keeps beating and raising: 2027 EPS of about $20 and NTM EPS of about $22.4 by late 2027. Labour scarcity supports pricing. The multiple drifts down to about 30-31x because of rates.

bull.story: Utility T&D capex above $170B/yr, the >$1.1T EEI large-load pipeline and the NiSource program entering backlog push backlog above $65B. Hyperscaler capex lands at Goldman's $1.2T rather than the $1.1T consensus. The premium multiple of about 38x on NTM EPS of $24 comes back.

thesis_break_reason: $470 is about 23-24x consensus 2027 EPS of $19.77, roughly the peer and pre-2023 multiple. Trading there would most likely mean the growth premium is broken: backlog falling quarter over quarter, a guidance cut, or utility or hyperscaler capex cuts. A 44%-vol name moving with the sector wouldn't normally get that low. The supervisor uses $455. I stay at $470 because with backlog +49% YoY, a ~29% fall from spot is hard to explain without a fundamental break, but $455-470 is a reasonable range.

key_uncertainties: How long AI capex keeps growing: consensus is ~$1.1T in 2027 (+~35%), UBS sees ~25% growth and Goldman ~54%. Direct exposure is only ~10% of revenue, but utility load growth adds indirect exposure.
Whether the multiple holds at 34x NTM vs. peers at 19-31x, with the Fed hiking (3.75-4.00%, more signalled)

reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $9.56B (+41%) and adjusted EPS $4.24. Backlog was a record $53.44B, +49% YoY vs $35.84B. Round 1 said +36%, which wrongly compared against the Sept-2025 figure. 12-month backlog is $32.3B, +61%. 2026 guidance was raised to $16.45-16.95 EPS and $2.0-2.5B FCF. Consensus is FY26 $16.73 and FY27 $19.77, with revisions 24 up and none down. Price path (corrected): the stock jumped +17.3% on the Q2 print, peaked at $722 on Aug 17, slid to $604 by Aug 25 on worries about leverage and valuation, and bounced to $662.60 after the Bernstein upgrade. The forward P/E went from ~50x in June to ~34x now. Round-2 changes. (a) I accepted the backlog correction and the ~10% direct data-center share from company commentary. Both support consensus EPS, so FY28E goes from $23.1 to $23.3. (b) The 54% figure for 2027 hyperscaler capex growth is relabelled as Goldman's above-consensus view; consensus is ~$1.1T (+~35%) and UBS sees ~25%. (c) I added the Sep 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, which I had missed. It is now the main reason the multiple compresses to 30x, replacing the discounted Substack ROIC claim. (d) Net debt goes from $5.6B to $5.9B because Enerfab closed after June 30. (e) I dropped the thin Polymarket recession market and the Kobeissi repost as inputs. Alternative signals still used: Revelio postings +52% (in line with the larger backlog and with crews being the bottleneck); the EEI large-load list (>$1.1T, 71 GW); low retail attention on AltIndex; Kalshi October FOMC odds of ~65/35 hold/hike (a liquid market). Valuation blends to ~$677, about spot. The stronger backlog and the rates headwind roughly cancel. Scenarios: bear 22% at $445, base 53% at $690, bull 25% at $920; mean ~$694. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (bear sigma 0.34, base and bull 0.21) shaded slightly down for rates, giving P(>= spot) of 0.55 (round 1: 0.568). Limits: X was not fetched directly, and the earnings date is unconfirmed.
